0: Knights by Minoru Murao (DMP) is a dark medieval fantasy adventure. In a land where the church burns suspected witches, the masked squire Mist, feared and hated by villagers as the Black Knight, works against the Saints behind the witch hunts. He travels with Euphemia, a young girl with a gift for brewing potions and poisons. It's a moody, action-driven read for fans of sword-and-sorcery with a grim edge.
2: Märchen by Hayate Kuku (Seven Seas) is a fantasy Boys' Love story built around a magical contract. An enchanted coat seals Sakim, the Divine Beast of the Moon, inside its magic circle, and when the summoner Gil inherits it, he gains command of Sakim. The pair set off together through wolf-filled forests, haunted towns, and bogs of the dead. It suits readers who like their romance wrapped in a dark fairy-tale journey.
3: Magika: Swordsman and Summoner by Mitsuki Mihara (Seven Seas) is a magic-school fantasy with plenty of action and comedy. Humanity has learned to call mythical beings from a parallel dimension, and fifteen-year-old Kazuki Hayashizaki becomes the first male summoner ever, enrolling at a school that has only ever admitted women. His sister, a magic swordswoman sworn to protect summoners, is dead set against it. It's a fit for fans of harem-flavored academy fantasy.
4: Cheeky Brat by Miyuki Mitsubachi (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny high school romance. Yuki Machida, the cool-headed manager of the basketball team, has spent years helping raise her five younger siblings and keeps her own feelings tucked away. She has a crush on the team captain, but a teasing underclassman, Sho Naruse, won't stop pursuing her. It's a warm pick for readers who love push-and-pull romances with a grounded heroine.
5: Dragon Hunter by Hong Seock Seo (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy action series steeped in folklore. In an ancient Korea terrorized by dragons, money-hungry hunter Seur Chong takes on the beasts with help from shamans, all while trying to live up to the legend of the great hunter Andrew Yi. Afflicted by the Dragon's Curse, he has to slay a blue dragon if he wants to survive. Expect brawling monster fights, roguish humor, and a mythic backdrop.
6: Dance in the Vampire Bund: Age of Scarlet Order by Nozomu Tamaki (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural sequel to the original vampire saga. In a United States gripped by vampire hunts, rumors spread that Mina Tepes will gather American vampires on the West Coast and carry them by ship to the Vampire Bund. But the Bund sank months ago, and Mina is said to be dead. It's for readers who want more gothic intrigue and action from the Bund's world.
7: Free Life Fantasy Online: Immortal Princess by Akisuzu Nenohi (Seven Seas) is a relaxed, funny VRMMO fantasy light novel. Gamer Kotone Tsukishiro gets a copy of Free Life Fantasy Online from her younger sister and picks one of its hardest inhuman races to play: a zombie. Her very first quest pulls her into a world that soon becomes a big part of her real life. It's a cozy pick for readers who enjoy game-world stories with an offbeat hero.
8: Phantom Busters by Neoshoco (Viz Media) is a lively supernatural comedy set at a high school. Top student Eugene Korekishi doesn't believe in ghosts, but his classmate Mogari Shishikuro is an exorcist who eats them. Since Mogari can't actually see ghosts himself, the two need someone with the sight, so they start a school exorcist club. It's a fun fit for fans of spooky buddy comedies with plenty of energy.
10: Yakuza Reincarnation by Takeshi Natsuhara and Hiroki Miyashita (Seven Seas) is a rowdy isekai action series with a tough-guy heart. An old-school yakuza is killed by young thugs while defending his turf and wakes up in a fantasy world as a young princess, Sanaria Ryu Lundberg, with his tattoo and strength intact. Now he may be the only one who can teach this world what yakuza honor means. It's great for readers who like brawls, gruff humor, and a fish-out-of-water lead.
12: Pastel by Toshihiko Kobayashi (Del Rey) is a gentle, comedic teen romance. After getting dumped, high schooler Mugi Mugimaru meets Yuu Tsukishima during a summer away and falls for her hard, only to find that she ends up living under the same roof as him. Their awkward closeness sets up plenty of misunderstandings and sweet moments. It's a good pick for fans of classic slice-of-life love stories with a soft, summery feel.
14: The World After the Fall by singNsong and Undead Gamja (Ize Press) is a big, brooding action fantasy adapted from the Korean web novel. Enormous towers appear around the world, swarms of monsters follow, and humanity's survival comes to rest on the Tower Walkers tasked with climbing to the top. Jaehwan begins to suspect the mission isn't what it seems and resolves to trust only himself on the way to Floor 100. It's for readers who like sprawling, philosophical battle stories with a lone-wolf hero.
16: Pokémon: Sword & Shield by Hidenori Kusaka and Satoshi Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a bright, kid-friendly adventure based on the Galar region video games. Casey Shield, a hacker who invented the Dynamax Simulator, wants to reunite with a lost Pokémon. Henry Sword, who repairs gear for Pokémon, is searching for the Rusted Sword and Rusted Shield. It's a great pick for young fans of the games and longtime Pokémon Adventures readers.
18: The Strange Adventure of a Broke Mercenary by Mine (Seven Seas) is a grounded sword-and-sorcery light novel. After the mercenaries who raised him die in a bloody battle, Loren is left with only his wits and his sword, so he turns to adventuring. His reckless new party treats him as a meat shield, and only their priest, Lapis, sees what he's worth. It's for readers who like a gruff, practical hero and a partnership that builds over time.
19: Angel Diary by Lee YunHee and Kara (Ice Kunion) is a lighthearted Korean fantasy romance. Dong-Hwa, a princess of Heaven, runs away to Earth to escape an arranged marriage to the King of Demons and hides out disguised as a high school boy. It isn't long before guardians from Heaven and the demon world come looking for her. It's a fun pick for fans of gender-bender comedy, lovely art, and celestial romance.
20: The Queen's Knight by Kim Kang-Won (Tokyopop) is a Korean portal fantasy with a romantic heart. As a girl, Yuna is rescued by a mysterious knight named Rieno, who swears to protect her. Years later she's drawn into his world, Phantasmagoria, where she's expected to take her place as its queen. It's for readers who like a fish-out-of-water heroine, a devoted protector, and plenty of court drama.
21: Crossplay Love: Otaku x Punk by Toru (Seven Seas) is a playful romantic comedy built on mistaken identities. Gloomy student Yuuma Hanae secretly works at a maid café as "Hana," and his delinquent schoolmate Shuumei Satogiri falls for Hana without knowing who she really is. Shuumei starts visiting the café dressed as a girl named Mei, and soon each is crushing on someone they think is a woman. It's a sweet, silly pick for fans of crossdressing comedies.
23: Into the Deepest, Most Unknowable Dungeon by Kakeru (Seven Seas) is an isekai fantasy adventure with a harem streak. After being hit by a truck, a former temp worker is reborn in another world as Jean, an average boy with no special abilities. Armed only with the practical know-how from his past life, he sets out to conquer the deepest, most mysterious dungeon in this new world. It's a fit for readers who like underdog heroes and dungeon crawling.
25: Mint Chocolate by Mami Orikasa (Yen Press) is a sweet and bittersweet high school romance. Nanami's longtime crush, suddenly becomes her stepbrother when their parents marry, and now she has to live with him under the same roof. His cold, arrogant attitude doesn't make things any easier. It's a cozy pick for fans of step-sibling romances and slow-thawing love interests.
26: Backstabbed in a Backwater Dungeon by Shisui Meikyou and Takafumi Oomae (Seven Seas) is a revenge-driven fantasy action series. Light is betrayed and left for dead by his adventuring party deep in a dungeon, but there he awakens an Infinite Gacha ability that summons allies at level 9999. With a loyal army at his back, he sets out to pay back everyone who wronged him. It's for readers who enjoy overpowered heroes and dark, satisfying payback stories.
27: His Majesty the Demon King's Housekeeper by Saiko Wadori and Mika Kajiyama (Seven Seas) is a charming isekai fantasy with a romantic thread. High schooler Sakura Takatsuki loves cleaning, so when she's swept into another world and lands in a realm ruled by a Demon King, she can't stand the grime. A witch's curse has blocked all cleaning magic there, so Sakura rolls up her sleeves and sets out to scrub the place clean herself. It's a gentle, upbeat read for fans of cozy fantasy.
29: iD_eNTITY by Hee-Joon Son and Youn-Kyung Kim (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy action series set inside an online game. Every night, Roto plays a virtual-reality game with two friends, and together they make a warrior, sorcerer, and healer team. Their in-game reputation has grown big enough to cause trouble for them, both inside the game and out. It's a fun read for gamers and fans of MMO adventures with a comedic edge.
30: Boys Be by Masahiro Itabashi (Tokyopop) is a sweet and comedic collection of teen romance stories. Each chapter follows a different high school boy as he works up the nerve to confess, stumbles through a first date, or wonders whether a girl he likes feels the same way. The stories are short, earnest, and often funny about the awkwardness of growing up. It's a nostalgic, easygoing read for fans of anthology-style love stories.
31: The Young Magician by Yuri Narushima (CMX) is a dark fantasy with an occult bent. Carno Guino is a magician whose soul is fused with demons, and Ibuki Shikishima is a Shinto practitioner, and the two young men are drawn into a tangled war between rival magical factions. Expect moody atmosphere, elegant art, and a slow-building partnership. It's a good fit for readers who like supernatural drama with plenty of mystery.
32: Species Domain by Shunsuke Noro (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy comedy set in a high school where elves, dwarves, and angels study alongside humans. Kazamori is an elf girl raised by humans who can't actually use magic, though everyone assumes she can. Her classmate Ohki, meanwhile, insists magic doesn't exist and everything can be explained by science. It's a funny, good-natured read for fans of slice-of-life school stories with a fantasy twist.
34: The Eccentric Doctor of the Moon Flower Kingdom by Tohru Himuka (Seven Seas) is a historical fantasy that mixes medical drama with romance. In the Moon Flower Kingdom, healing has long relied on superstition, and Prince Keiun is looking for something better. When his party is attacked, he watches an unusual teenage girl named Koyou perform a lifesaving procedure. It's for readers who enjoy clever heroines, court intrigue, and stories in the spirit of The Apothecary Diaries.
35: My Special One by Momoko Koda (Viz Media) is a sweet and funny shojo romance. After a humiliating rejection, Sahoko Wakaume swears she'll never fall for a good-looking guy again. So when idol Kouta Kirigaya starts showing up at her family's restaurant, she gives him the cold shoulder, even as she slowly begins to warm up to him. It's a light, heartfelt pick for fans of celebrity romances and down-to-earth heroines.
37: Phantom Tales of the Night by Matsuri (Yen Press) is a dark supernatural fantasy with a mysterious edge. The Murakumo Inn serves both humans and non-humans, and instead of payment, its enigmatic owner asks each guest for a deeply shameful secret. High schooler Tokihito Sasaki learns he has been dead for a long time and was revived by the owner as a living corpse. Fans of xxxHolic and Hell Girl will enjoy its eerie, elegant mood.
38: Today's Cerberus by Ato Sakurai (Yen Press) is a supernatural comedy with a harem twist. As a child, Chiaki Mikado was bitten by a three-headed dog, and he has been listless ever since. Then his father sends him Kuro from Greece, who says she's there to protect him; she turns out to be one of three girls who together make up Cerberus, and they move in with Chiaki to make amends. It's light, silly fun for fans of mythological romcoms.
39: Kamui by Shingo Nanami (Broccoli Books) is a sweeping shonen action fantasy. When the sacred spirit Okikurumi is stolen from Atsuma's village, the kamui spirits fall into chaos and the world itself is threatened. Atsuma, carrying the spirit of an ancient sword, leaves home to get it back and joins NOA, a group of youths who wield kamui power. It's a good pick for fans of spirit-powered battles and quest stories.
40: Snow Drop by Choi Kyung-ah (Tokyopop) is a heartfelt Korean romance with a dramatic streak. After a painful past, Yoo So-na finds comfort in tending the flowers at her family's nursery. Back at high school, she meets Oh Hae-gi, a teen model, and the two bond over the hurts they both carry, even as their families push back against the relationship. It's a good pick for readers who love emotional, melodramatic first-love stories.
41: Kamen Rider Kuuga by Toshiki Inoue and Hitotsu Yokoshima (Titan Manga) is a grown-up reimagining of the classic tokusatsu hero. When the ancient Grongi tribe awakens and begins killing people in modern Japan, a cheerful wanderer named Yusuke Godai finds a mysterious belt that transforms him into the warrior Kuuga. Working alongside detective Kaoru Ichijo, he takes on the monsters one battle at a time. It's a strong pick for longtime Rider fans and newcomers who like gritty hero action.
43: Succubus and Hitman by Makoto Fukami and Seigo Tokiya (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural revenge story. High schooler Gamou Shouya is, in a sense, already dead: his body now holds the soul of a boy who made a pact with the succubus Armelina. He works as her hitman, and in return she helps him hunt down the people who murdered him and his family. It's for readers who like grim, stylish action with a demonic partnership at its core.
45: Gacha Gacha by Hiroyuki Tamakoshi (Del Rey) is a lively romantic comedy with a gaming twist. Kouhei has long had a crush on his sweet, studious classmate Kurara, but an encounter with a video game leaves her with several different personalities that pop out without warning. Kouhei ends up keeping her secret and trying to manage the chaos. It's a breezy read for fans of romcoms full of mix-ups and misunderstandings.
46: Monster Guild: The Dark Lord's (No-Good) Comeback! by Tourou (Seven Seas) is a goofy fantasy comedy told from the villain's side. After being defeated by a hero who just won't stay dead, the once all-powerful Dark Lord survives only by splitting off a sliver of his soul, leaving him weaker than a slime. To reclaim his throne, he starts building a guild of monsters from the ground up. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy fantasy parodies and underdog villains.
47: Am I Actually the Strongest? by Sai Sumimori and Ai Takahashi (Kodansha) is a lighthearted isekai fantasy comedy. Reborn as Haruto, a baby prince in a world of magic, the hero is judged to have no magical talent and is cast out of the royal family. In truth he's absurdly powerful, and he would much rather live a quiet life than let anyone find out. It's an easygoing pick for fans of overpowered heroes and gentle, comic adventures.
48: Nora: The Last Chronicle of Devildom by Kazunari Kakei (Viz Media) is a high-energy supernatural action comedy. Nora is a delinquent demon whose true form is Cerberus, a vicious hound of disaster, but he can only use his magic with permission from Kazuma, a human student who is very reluctant to give it. The Dark Liege wants the mismatched pair to team up against renegade demons in the human world. It's a fun read for fans of bickering-partner battle manga.
49: Beauty and the Feast by Satomi U (Square Enix Manga) is a warm, food-centered romantic comedy. Shuuko Yakumo, a 28-year-old widow, has been drifting through life until Shohei Yamato, a 15-year-old high school baseball recruit, moves in next door. Noticing that he lives on convenience store food and has an enormous appetite, she starts cooking him dinner, and her love of cooking slowly returns. It's a cozy, gentle pick for fans of slice-of-life stories built around home-cooked meals.
50: One by Lee Vin (Tokyopop) is a Korean music-industry drama with a romantic thread. In public, high schooler Jenny You is a pop princess, but in private she's a rebellious beauty her classmates shun. Her quiet classmate Eumpa Won, nicknamed "One," gave up his childhood fame as a musical prodigy in the United States to live an ordinary life, until his music teacher steals his work and passes it off as his own. It's for readers who love stories about talent, fame, and first love.
51: Black Night Parade by Hikaru Nakamura (Seven Seas) is an offbeat supernatural comedy with a dark streak. Hino Miharu works a dead-end convenience store job and spends Christmas alone, until a run-in with a shadowy Black Santa, the one who deals with bad children, gets him whisked off to the Arctic. There he's hired into a sprawling Christmas operation that may be a dream job or a nightmare. It's for readers who like cynical, quirky humor and a holiday story with a twist.
52: Blade of Heaven by Yong-su Hwang and Kyung-il Yang (Tokyopop) is a Korean martial arts fantasy full of action and humor, drawn from Asian myth and legend. Young Soma is accused by the King of Heaven of stealing his sword, and he sets out with Princess Aroomee and General Winter to track down the legendary Blade of Heaven. It's a fun pick for fans of energetic sword fights and mythic adventures.
53: Blazin' Barrels by Min-Seo Park (Tokyopop) is a Korean action comedy set in a futuristic Wild West. Sting looks harmless and naive, but he's a skilled fighter with dreams of becoming a bounty hunter. When he spots a bounty for Gold Romany, an all-girl gang of outlaws, he figures capturing them is his ticket to fame and fortune. It's a rowdy, good-humored read for fans of gunslinger adventures and goofy heroes.
56: Jack Frost by JinHo Ko (Yen Press) is a Korean supernatural action series with a horror edge. Noh-A Joo is a new student at Amityville High School, and she quickly learns the school is not what it seems. She's pulled into a war between vampires, monsters, and other creatures, and has to figure out her role as a "mirror image" while dealing with the mysterious Jack Frost. It's for readers who like bloody, stylish battles and dark mysteries.
57: Karate Survivor in Another World by Yazin and Takahito Kobayashi (Seven Seas) is a scrappy isekai survival adventure. A martial artist is reborn in a fantasy world after a clumsy deity drops him deep in a wild forest. With no magic and no cheat skills, he has nothing to rely on but his wits and his karate. It's a fun change of pace for readers who like grounded, hand-to-hand action and a hero who earns every win the hard way.
58: Ragnarok by Lee Myung-Jin (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy adventure rooted in Norse mythology. Chaos is an amnesiac warrior living in the village of Fayon, while the fierce Fenris searches for the reincarnation of the god Balder in order to bring about Ragnarok. What follows is a sweeping tale full of swordplay, gods, and monsters. It's a natural pick for fans of the Ragnarok Online game and anyone who likes old-school high-fantasy action.
59: Knight of the Ice by Yayoi Ogawa (Kodansha) is a funny, warmhearted romance set in the world of figure skating. Kokoro Kijinami is an internationally celebrated skater famous for his elegant, knightly performances, but off the ice he's a hopeless romantic and an anime fan. He can only land his quad jumps when his childhood friend Chitose is nearby to recite a spell from a magical girl show. It's a delight for fans of sports romance and quirky couples.
60: Yokai Cats by Pandania (Seven Seas) is a playful, full-color comedy about pet cats with a secret. These seemingly ordinary house cats are actually supernatural yokai who can stretch their necks to swipe food off the counter or turn into a giant wall to block your path. The series turns everyday cat mischief into folklore-flavored fun. It's a family-friendly pick for cat lovers of all ages.
63: Zo Zo Zombie by Yasunari Nagatoshi (JY) is a silly, kid-friendly horror comedy. Fifth grader Isamu goes looking for the zombie rumored to haunt a playground and finds Zombie Boy asleep in the sandbox. Zombie Boy can swap his blood for tomato juice and pop his limbs off and on, and he'd much rather be friends than eat brains, though his weird antics keep landing Isamu in trouble. It's a great fit for young readers who love gross-out gags and slapstick.
64: Enchanter by Izumi Kawachi (DMP) is a supernatural romantic comedy. In a world where enchanters craft magical items using power from contracted demons, high schooler Haruhiko Kanou is approached by the demon Eukanaria, who wants to revive her lost love, the enchanter Fulcanelli, by placing his soul in Haruhiko's body. Haruhiko, meanwhile, has a secret crush on his childhood friend Yuka. It's a lighthearted pick for fans of love triangles with a magical twist.
65: Sorry for My Familiar by Tekka Yaguraba (Seven Seas) is a goofy fantasy comedy about a mismatched pair of travelers. A young demon girl ends up with a familiar who is anything but ordinary: an eccentric older man and mad monster researcher whose obsession with creatures makes him a handful. The two set out on the road together, and his enthusiasm keeps dragging them into trouble. It's a fun read for fans of offbeat fantasy humor and odd-couple adventures.
66: Spirits and Cat Ears by Miyuki Nakayama (Yen Press) is a cozy supernatural comedy with a romantic heart. Neneko Izuna, a young but experienced shrine maiden, and her shikigami partner, Sagami Shichikage, move to the Waka Clinic to help exorcise evil spirits. The story follows their everyday lives and spirit-busting jobs as a gentle romance grows between them. It's a sweet pick for readers who like cat-eared spirits, folklore, and slice-of-life charm.
67: Anyway, I'm Falling in Love with You. by Haruka Mitsui (Kodansha) is a heartfelt shojo romance about childhood friends on the edge of growing up. Mizuho dreams of watching the summer fireworks with the right person, and several boys are drawn to her, including her childhood friend Kizuki and the brainy future doctor Shin. All the while, she worries that growing up will pull her and her friends apart. It's a lovely pick for fans of love triangles and bittersweet youth.
68: Steel of the Celestial Shadows by Daruma Matsuura (Viz Media) is a strange and inventive samurai adventure. Konosuke is a samurai cursed so that metal repels him, leaving him unable to wield a sword. Despairing, he resolves to die, but a woman saves him and, to his surprise, proposes marriage. It's for readers who enjoy historical action with a supernatural twist, offbeat humor, and an unusual couple at its center.
70: Futaribeya: A Room for Two by Yukiko (Tokyopop) is a gentle yuri slice-of-life story. Responsible Sakurako Kawawa is about to start high school and moves into a school boarding house, where she's paired with roommate Kasumi Yamabuki, an easygoing girl who puts minimal effort into just about everything. Despite their opposite personalities, the two slowly grow close. It's a soft, cozy read for fans of quiet roommate stories and sweet, low-key romance.
71: Monster Hunter: Flash Hunter by Keiichi Hikami and Shin Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a fast-paced action fantasy based on Capcom's hit game series. In a world ruled by monsters, humanity depends on elite hunters for protection. Raiga and his friends are hunters too, but early on they're still inexperienced, and their first clash with a dragon-like monster shows them that poor teamwork could get them killed. It's a great pick for fans of the games and big monster battles.
72: The Dragon Knight's Beloved by Asagi Orikawa and Ritsu Aozaki (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy romance with plenty of dragons. On her sixteenth birthday, Melissa takes a job as a maid at the royal castle to be closer to the dragons and to her idol, Dragon Knight Captain Hubert. When she learns he's about to retire, she fears she's missed her chance, and then he asks her to be his pretend girlfriend. It's a cozy pick for fans of fake-dating romances.
73: Neck and Neck by Lee Sun-Hee (Tokyopop) is a Korean high school romance with a crime-family twist. Dabin Choi is the daughter of Seoul's most powerful crime boss, and she has a crush on Eugene, the son of one of her father's associates, who only sees her as a little sister. When a new classmate turns out to be the son of her father's longtime rival, school becomes a battleground of power games. It's a fun pick for fans of feisty heroines and dramatic love triangles.
74: He's My Only Vampire by Aya Shouoto (Yen Press) is a dark, romantic supernatural drama. Kana was once a gifted long jumper until a leg injury ended her athletic future, and her former teammates now accuse her of faking her pain. When she's badly hurt saving a little girl from a traffic accident, a boy she played with as a child reappears, reveals he's a vampire, and binds her to him to save her life. It's for readers who like brooding paranormal romance with a gothic mood.
75: Not Lives by Wataru Karasuma (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi action series set around a deadly game. Mikami Shigeru is a gamer and aspiring game designer who dreams of creating the ultimate gaming experience. When he finds a mysterious disc among some research materials, it implants itself in his body, and he begins seeing the world through his cool-headed game avatar, Kyouka. Now the two have to survive a game with real-world consequences. It's for fans of high-stakes game-world thrillers.
77: PhD: Phantasy Degree by Hee-Joon Son (Tokyopop) is a lively Korean fantasy comedy. Sang is a spunky girl searching for the Demon School Hades, a place no ordinary human is supposed to set foot in. Once she finds her way in, she falls in with a band of misfit monsters and gets swept up in the hunt for the mysterious Satan's Rings. It's a fun pick for fans of monster-school mischief, slapstick humor, and energetic art.
78: Pieces of a Spiral by Kaimu Tachibana (CMX) is a supernatural action fantasy steeped in reincarnation and old loyalties. Sakuya and Wakyo are reunited in a new life, only to learn that Bishu, their former master, is in danger from demons seeking revenge. They have to protect him before those dark forces take hold of his new life. It's a good pick for readers who like moody demon-hunting stories, devoted partnerships, and elegant shojo-style art.
79: Tokyo Aliens by Naoe (Square Enix) is a stylish sci-fi action series with a mystery at its core. Akira Gunji is an ordinary first-year high school student who hopes to follow his late father into the police force. After witnessing a fight between two people with strange powers on a train, he's abducted by an alien and learns some unsettling truths about his father. It's a fun read for fans of superpowered action and alien conspiracies.
80: Wild Act by Rie Takada (Tokyopop) is a bubbly shojo romance set in the world of acting. Fifteen-year-old Yuniko Sakuraba is so devoted to the late actor Akira Nanae that she'll go to wild lengths to collect his belongings. Her obsession brings her face to face with Ryu Eba, a hot young actor and rival in more ways than one. It's a fun, fast-paced pick for fans of showbiz romance and feisty heroines.
81: Sand Chronicles by Hinako Ashihara (Viz Media) is a moving shojo coming-of-age drama. After her parents divorce, twelve-year-old Ann Uekusa moves with her mother from Tokyo to her mother's hometown in rural Shimane. There she meets Daigo, a local boy, and siblings Fuji and Shika, and the story follows their friendships and first loves as they grow up. It's a beautiful, emotional pick for readers who love character-driven stories that span years.
82: Seimaden by You Higuri (CMX) is a lush gothic fantasy romance. The demon prince Laures loves Hilda, a human dancer who is the reincarnation of his former lover, Ellis, for whom he once gave up his humanity. Hilda knows nothing of her past and finds herself torn between Laures and Roderique, while Laures' loyal deputy schemes to drag him back to the demon world. It's for readers who love dramatic, beautifully drawn tales of forbidden love.
83: Love and Heart by Chitose Kaidou (Yen Press) is a quirky shojo romance with a mysterious edge. After catching her boyfriend cheating, Yoh breaks up with him and wants nothing to do with love. Then Haruma Hirose, a boy from across the street, turns up inside her house with a key her mother gave him, and Yoh starts to suspect he might be a stalker. It's a fun pick for readers who like offbeat romcoms with a slightly eerie love interest.
84: Dragon Voice by Yuriko Nishiyama (Tokyopop) is an upbeat comedy-drama about chasing a dream in the music world. Rin Amami has always loved to sing, but his unusual, gravelly voice gets him laughed at. His big break comes when a boy band takes notice of him. It's a fun pick for readers who like underdog stories, idol-industry drama, and big dreams.
85: Et Cetera by Tow Nakazaki (Tokyopop) is a rollicking action adventure set in an alternate American West. Mingchao, an orphaned girl from China, inherits the Eto gun, which fires bullets powered by the essences of the Chinese zodiac animals. She sets off across the country with a priest named Baskerville to uncover the gun's dark origins, while a crime syndicate hunts the weapon. It's a great pick for fans of gunslinging Westerns with a fantasy twist.
86: Silver Diamond by Shiho Sugiura (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy adventure with a warm heart. Rakan Akatsuki is an orphaned boy with a rare gift for making plants grow. One day a mysterious young man named Chigusa appears in his garden from another world, and Rakan's quiet life gives way to dangers and new allies. It's a good fit for readers who like soft, character-driven fantasy and found-family bonds.
87: So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? by Nazuna Miki and Tsukasa Araki (Yen Press) is a cheerful isekai fantasy comedy. Salaryman Akira Yagami dies saving a boy from a truck and is reborn as a goblin in another world. Goblins usually live only about seven days, but somehow he's inherited an unusually long lifespan, and he sets out to make the most of it. It's an easygoing read for fans of monster-reincarnation stories with a light touch.
89: Of the Red, the Light, and the Ayakashi by HaccaWorks* and Nanao (Yen Press) is an atmospheric supernatural mystery based on a visual novel. Yue has been raised in a Shinto shrine on a mountain and is forbidden to leave or see the outside world. When he visits the town's winter festival with his childhood friend, the black fox Kurogitsune, almost everyone looks like a shadow to him, except for two mysterious boys. It's for readers who like eerie folklore and puzzle-box storytelling.
90: Smokin' Parade by Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou (Yen Press) is a gory, high-octane action horror series from the creators of Deadman Wonderland. The Amenotori company has developed technology that can transplant any body part, and Youkou Kakujou's formerly wheelchair-bound sister is one of its success stories. Meanwhile, the area is plagued by grisly killings tied to people in animal-head costumes, and the siblings are pulled into the violence alongside a cyborg team called the Jackolopes. It's for readers with a strong stomach.
91: Love and Heart by Chitose Kaidou (Yen Press) is a quirky shojo romance with a mysterious edge. After catching her boyfriend cheating, Yoh breaks up with him and wants nothing to do with love. Then Haruma Hirose, a boy from across the street, turns up inside her house with a key her mother gave him, and Yoh starts to suspect he might be a stalker. It's a fun pick for readers who like offbeat romcoms with a slightly eerie love interest.
93: After God by Sumi Eno (Viz Media) is a haunting supernatural action story set in a ravaged Japan. Gods have invaded the country, leaving death and destruction behind and turning whole cities into uninhabitable danger zones. Anti-God researcher Sachiyuki Tokinaga is determined to find a way to defeat them, and his path soon crosses with high schooler Waka Kamikura. It's for readers who like eerie, beautifully drawn stories built around one big question: how do you kill a god?
94: Pass the Monster Meat, Milady! by Sakae Esuno (Kodansha) is a cheerful fantasy romcom with a big appetite. Noble lady Melphiera has a secret passion for monsters, and especially for cooking and eating them. When her engagement falls through, she accepts a proposal from the feared "Bloody Duke" Aldo, whose lands happen to be teeming with monsters. It's a delightful pick for fans of foodie fantasy and offbeat, sweet couples.
95: Tune In to the Midnight Heart by Masakuni Igarashi (Kodansha) is an upbeat romantic comedy. Years ago, Arisu Yamabuki was comforted by the livestreams of a mysterious girl called Apollo, and he's never forgotten her voice. After tracing her to a particular high school, he transfers there and discovers she must be one of the four girls in the broadcasting club, so he sets out to find out which one while helping each of them chase her dreams. It's a fun pick for fans of harem romcoms.
96: Nue's Exorcist by Kota Kawae (Viz Media) is a punchy supernatural action series. Gakuro Yakushiji is a timid boy who has been bullied for years, until he stumbles on a mysterious shrine and unseals Nue, a powerful and arrogant yokai. Bound together, the two take on the demons hiding in the human world. It's a fun pick for fans of exorcist battles, monster partners, and underdog heroes.
97: A Tale of the Secret Saint ZERO by Touya and Chibi (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy prequel light novel. Three hundred years before Fia's adventures, Princess Serafina lives hidden away in a forest with the forest spirits and her cousin, the young knight captain Sirius Ulysses. When an incident awakens mysterious powers inside her, she takes her first steps on the path to becoming the Great Saint. It's a treat for fans of the main series who want to see where the legend began.
98: My Kitten is a Picky Eater by Migiri Miki (Seven Seas) is a gentle, heartwarming slice-of-life comedy. A kind young man named Taiyo Mano rescues a kitten from the snow and names her Yuki. As a first-time pet owner, he quickly discovers that Yuki turns up her nose at store-bought cat food, so he teaches himself to cook to make meals she'll actually eat. It's a cozy pick for cat lovers and fans of comforting food stories.
99: Game of Familia by Mikoto Yamaguchi and D.P (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy adventure built around a blended family. Shy high schooler Sasae Hatsushima feels ordinary next to his accomplished stepfamily, and after his father dies just months into the remarriage, Sasae is pulled into another world with his stepmother Kanae and stepsisters Manako and Hinana. There they're asked to defeat an army of the undead. It's for readers who like isekai with real stakes and family drama.
